items.title: Kyushu University achieves 130% quantum yield in solar breakthrough

featured_image.name: Singlet fission breaks 'ceiling' of solar cells for 130% quantum yield

items.description: A flurry of breakthroughs in solar cell research is challenging assumptions about how much energy photovoltaic technology can extract from sunlight. In findings published this week, researchers at Kyushu University in Japan and Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz in Germany achieved a quantum yield of roughly 130 percent — meaning more energy carriers were produced than photons absorbed — while a separate team at the Chinese Academy of Sciences reached a power conversion efficiency of 29.76 percent for all-perovskite tandem solar cells.

items.title: Houthis enter Iran war as attacks sweep Gulf states

featured_image.name: At least 15 US troops wounded in Iran strike on Saudi airbase: Reports

items.description:
An Iranian missile and drone attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia on Friday wounded at least 12 American service members and damaged multiple U.S. military aircraft, marking one of the most serious breaches of American air defenses since the war began a month ago. Two of the wounded were listed in serious condition, according to U.S. officials cited by The New York Times and Reuters.[1][2]

The assault on the base south of Riyadh involved ballistic missiles and drones, with at least two missiles and one drone bypassing U.S. air defenses, according to officials. Multiple KC-135 aerial refueling tankers were damaged, and an E-3 Sentry AWACS command-and-control aircraft also sustained damage, Air & Space Forces Magazine reported. Iran publicized satellite imagery it said showed burning aircraft at the base. By Saturday, the total number of injuries had risen to around two dozen, with most of the additional cases attributed to traumatic brain injuries, according to The New York Times.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: Vance says US will leave Iran 'soon' as Tehran rejects peace talks

featured_image.name: JD Vance is walking a tightrope on Iran. What does he really think?

items.description:
Vice President JD Vance said on Saturday that the United States has achieved most of its military objectives in Iran and plans to leave "soon," even as Tehran publicly denies that any meaningful peace negotiations are underway, one month into the conflict that has roiled global energy markets.

Speaking in an interview with conservative podcaster Benny Johnson, Vance acknowledged the war's economic toll but framed it as fleeting. "This is a very, very temporary reaction to what is ultimately going to be a short-term conflict," he said, referring to soaring energy prices caused by the near-total closure of the Strait of Hormuz. He added that President Trump "has been very clear" the administration has no interest in a prolonged presence: "We're not interested in being in Iran a year down the road, two years down the road. We're taking care of business, we're going to be out of there soon, and gas prices are going to come back down."[1][2][3]

Yet Vance also signaled that the campaign is not over. "The president's going to keep at it for a little while longer to ensure that once we leave, we don't have to do this again for a very, very long time," he said. "We need to neuter them for a very, very long time, and that's the purpose."[1]

items.title: Houthis launch first missile attack on Israel as U.S. Marines reach Middle East

featured_image.name: U.S. to Deploy Marines to Middle East. Here's What They Could Be ...

items.description:
The USS Tripoli and roughly 2,500 Marines arrived in the Middle East on Friday as Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen launched their first missile attack on Israel since the war began, opening a new front in a rapidly expanding regional conflict now one month old.

U.S. Central Command announced Saturday that the Tripoli Amphibious Ready Group and the embarked 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit reached its area of responsibility on March 27, carrying approximately 3,500 sailors and Marines along with strike fighter aircraft and amphibious assault assets. The America-class amphibious assault ship had departed its homeport of Sasebo, Japan, earlier this month after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth approved a CENTCOM request for reinforcements.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: WHO says nine paramedics killed in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israel Killed Over a Dozen Lebanese Paramedics in Three Days ...

items.description:
The World Health Organization said Saturday that nine paramedics were killed and seven others wounded in five separate attacks on healthcare teams in southern Lebanon, bringing the total number of health workers killed since the Israeli military escalation began on March 2 to 51.[1][2]

WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus detailed the strikes in a post on X, saying medics were hit while on duty in five villages. In Zoutar al-Sharqiya, five health workers were killed and two injured, one critically. Two more were killed and three wounded in Kfar Tibnit. One paramedic died in each of Ghandouriyeh and Jezzine, while two were wounded in Kfar Dajjal.[2][3]

"The repeated attacks on health care are severely disrupting the delivery of services in southern Lebanon," Tedros wrote, adding that "the only way to end these tragedies is to end attacks on health care, NOW".[2]
